claim: A genetic analysis of sRNA abundance in flag leaf from an immortalized F2 (IMF2) population in rice was performed.
source: We performed a genetic analysis of sRNA abundance in flag leaf from an immortalized F2 (IMF2) population in rice.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as the main objective of the study.

claim: 53,613,739 unique sRNAs were identified.
source: We identified 53,613,739 unique sRNAs and 165,797 sRNA expression traits (s-traits).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative result from the data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: 165,797 sRNA expression traits (s-traits) were identified.
source: We identified 53,613,739 unique sRNAs and 165,797 sRNA expression traits (s-traits).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative result from the data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: 66,649 s-traits mapped 40,049 local-sQTLs and 30,809 distant-sQTLs.
source: A total of 66,649 s-traits mapped 40,049 local-sQTLs and 30,809 distant-sQTLs.
evidence: This is a direct quantitative result from the QTL mapping analysis.

claim: 80,362 sRNA clusters were defined.
source: By defining 80,362 sRNA clusters, 22,263 sRNA cluster QTLs (scQTLs) were recovered for 20,249 of all the 50,139 sRNA cluster expression traits (sc-traits).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative result from the sRNA cluster analysis.

claim: 22,263 sRNA cluster QTLs (scQTLs) were recovered for 20,249 of all the 50,139 sRNA cluster expression traits (sc-traits).
source: By defining 80,362 sRNA clusters, 22,263 sRNA cluster QTLs (scQTLs) were recovered for 20,249 of all the 50,139 sRNA cluster expression traits (sc-traits).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative result from the QTL mapping analysis of sRNA clusters.

claim: The expression levels for most of s-traits from the same genes or the same sRNA clusters were slightly positively correlated.
source: The expression levels for most of s-traits from the same genes or the same sRNA clusters were slightly positively correlated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from correlation analysis of expression data.

claim: Genetic co-regulation between sRNAs from the same mother genes and between sRNAs and their mother genes was observed for a portion of the sRNAs.
source: While genetic co-regulation between sRNAs from the same mother genes and between sRNAs and their mother genes was observed for a portion of the sRNAs, most of the sRNAs and their mother genes showed little co-regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from QTL mapping and correlation analysis.

claim: Most of the sRNAs and their mother genes showed little co-regulation.
source: While genetic co-regulation between sRNAs from the same mother genes and between sRNAs and their mother genes was observed for a portion of the sRNAs, most of the sRNAs and their mother genes showed little co-regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from QTL mapping and correlation analysis.

claim: Some sRNA biogenesis genes were located in distant-sQTL hotspots and showed correspondence with specific length classes of sRNAs suggesting their important roles in the regulation and biogenesis of the sRNAs.
source: Some sRNA biogenesis genes were located in distant-sQTL hotspots and showed correspondence with specific length classes of sRNAs suggesting their important roles in the regulation and biogenesis of the sRNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of QTL hotspots and their overlap with sRNA biogenesis genes.

claim: Small RNAs (sRNAs) are non-coding RNAs mainly 18–30 nt in length that regulate a wide range of biological processes in eukaryotic organisms.
source: Small RNAs (sRNAs) are non-coding RNAs mainly 18–30 nt in length that regulate a wide range of biological processes in eukaryotic organisms (Carthew and Sontheimer, 2009; Axtell, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: sRNAs can be grouped into two major types: hpRNAs that are derived from single-stranded precursors with a hairpin structure (such as microRNAs [miRNAs]) and short interfering RNA (siRNAs) that are derived from double-stranded RNA precursors.
source: According to their origin, sRNAs can be grouped into two major types: hpRNAs that are derived from single-stranded precursors with a hairpin structure (such as microRNAs [miRNAs]) and short interfering RNA (siRNAs) that are derived from double-stranded RNA precursors such as heterochromatic small interfering RNAs (hc-siRNA) and trans-acting siRNAs (ta-siRNA).
evidence: This is established knowledge about sRNA classification.

claim: In plants, sRNAs function in regulating growth, development, architecture, yield, and response to biotic and abiotic stresses.
source: In plants, sRNAs function in regulating growth, development (Juarez et al., 2004; Zhu and Helliwell, 2011), architecture (Jiao et al., 2010; Miura et al., 2010), yield (Zhang et al., 2013), and response to biotic and abiotic stresses (Lu et al., 2008; Shukla et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: sRNA regulations are usually achieved by mediating endogenous mRNA cleavage and decay, DNA methylation of source and target loci, and chromatin modification and transcriptional silencing.
source: Such regulations are usually achieved by mediating endogenous mRNA cleavage and decay, DNA methylation of source and target loci, and chromatin modification and transcriptional silencing (Arikit et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The pathways for sRNA biogenesis and functioning from precursor transcription, processing, maturation, and action are relatively conserved.
source: Although the sRNAs differ in length, sequences, and functions, the pathways for their biogenesis and functioning from precursor transcription, processing, maturation, and action are relatively conserved, which involve the activities of a number of enzymes including RNA polymerase II (Pol II), RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RDRs), Dicer-like proteins (DCLs), and Argonautes (AGOs) (Chen, 2009; Ghildiyal and Zamore, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The abundance of sRNA species can be highly variable among individuals within a species.
source: It is also known that the abundance of sRNA species can be highly variable among individuals within a species, and the possible regulatory role of such quantitative difference has been assumed (He et al., 2010; Groszmann et al., 2011b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The quantitative variation of sRNA species between genotypes has not been assayed at the population level and their genetic control has yet to be elucidated.
source: It is not known whether the quantitative variation of sRNA species between genotypes is related to the biological machinery, as quantitative variation of sRNAs has not been assayed at the population level and their genetic control has yet to be elucidated.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The genetic materials consisted of 98 hybrids obtained by paired crosses of 196 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) derived by single seed descent from a cross between Zhenshan 97 and Minghui 63.
source: The genetic materials consisted of 98 hybrids obtained by paired crosses of 196 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) derived by single seed descent from a cross between Zhenshan 97 and Minghui 63, the parents of Shanyou 63 that was the most widely cultivated rice hybrid in the 1980s and 1990s and still used with reduced area in recent years in China.
evidence: This describes the experimental materials used in the study.

claim: Shanyou 63 was the most widely cultivated rice hybrid in the 1980s and 1990s and still used with reduced area in recent years in China.
source: The genetic materials consisted of 98 hybrids obtained by paired crosses of 196 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) derived by single seed descent from a cross between Zhenshan 97 and Minghui 63, the parents of Shanyou 63 that was the most widely cultivated rice hybrid in the 1980s and 1990s and still used with reduced area in recent years in China.
evidence: This is background information about the rice hybrid used in the study.

claim: The numbers of resulting reads varied from 14.52 million to 27.73 million per library (2.08 billion in total).
source: The numbers of resulting reads varied from 14.52 million to 27.73 million per library (2.08 billion in total) with non-redundant reads ranging from 3.00 million to 6.86 million per library (0.52 billion in total) (Supplementary file 1 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015], Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequencing data.

claim: Non-redundant reads ranged from 3.00 million to 6.86 million per library (0.52 billion in total).
source: The numbers of resulting reads varied from 14.52 million to 27.73 million per library (2.08 billion in total) with non-redundant reads ranging from 3.00 million to 6.86 million per library (0.52 billion in total) (Supplementary file 1 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015], Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequencing data.

claim: The 24 nt sRNAs were the most numerous in both redundant and distinct reads.
source: The 24 nt sRNAs were the most numerous in both redundant and distinct reads (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the data analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Approximately 82.28% of the sRNAs had identical sequences between parents.
source: The reads could be divided into four categories: (1) approximately 82.28% of the sRNAs had identical sequences between parents, (2) 0.71% of the sRNAs had SNPs between the two parents, (3) 8.35% were only mapped to the Zhenshan 97 genome, and (4) 8.66% were specifically mapped to the Minghui 63 genome (Supplementary file 2 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mapping analysis.

claim: 0.71% of the sRNAs had SNPs between the two parents.
source: The reads could be divided into four categories: (1) approximately 82.28% of the sRNAs had identical sequences between parents, (2) 0.71% of the sRNAs had SNPs between the two parents, (3) 8.35% were only mapped to the Zhenshan 97 genome, and (4) 8.66% were specifically mapped to the Minghui 63 genome (Supplementary file 2 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mapping analysis.

claim: 8.35% of sRNAs were only mapped to the Zhenshan 97 genome.
source: The reads could be divided into four categories: (1) approximately 82.28% of the sRNAs had identical sequences between parents, (2) 0.71% of the sRNAs had SNPs between the two parents, (3) 8.35% were only mapped to the Zhenshan 97 genome, and (4) 8.66% were specifically mapped to the Minghui 63 genome (Supplementary file 2 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mapping analysis.

claim: 8.66% of sRNAs were specifically mapped to the Minghui 63 genome.
source: The reads could be divided into four categories: (1) approximately 82.28% of the sRNAs had identical sequences between parents, (2) 0.71% of the sRNAs had SNPs between the two parents, (3) 8.35% were only mapped to the Zhenshan 97 genome, and (4) 8.66% were specifically mapped to the Minghui 63 genome (Supplementary file 2 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mapping analysis.

claim: Approximately 84.7% of sRNAs were found in no more than 5 IMF2s.
source: Approximately 84.7% of sRNAs were found in no more than 5 IMF2s, while only 0.13% were present in all 98 IMF2s (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Only 0.13% of sRNAs were present in all 98 IMF2s.
source: Approximately 84.7% of sRNAs were found in no more than 5 IMF2s, while only 0.13% were present in all 98 IMF2s (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Approximately 51.1% of sRNAs originated from the 2-kb upstream and the genic regions of non-transposon genes.
source: Approximately 51.1% of sRNAs originated from the 2-kb upstream and the genic regions of non-transposon genes (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the genomic distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: About 34.4% of sRNAs originated from intergenic regions, which account for no more than 20% of the whole genome length.
source: About 34.4% of sRNAs originated from intergenic regions, which account for no more than 20% of the whole genome length (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the genomic distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: About 43.9% of sRNAs were 24 nt.
source: About 43.9% of sRNAs were 24 nt, while 12.1% were 21 nt (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the size distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: 12.1% of sRNAs were 21 nt.
source: About 43.9% of sRNAs were 24 nt, while 12.1% were 21 nt (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the size distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The genic regions of non-transposon genes held the highest number of 21 nt sRNAs.
source: The genic regions of non-transposon genes held the highest number of 21 nt sRNAs, while 24 nt sRNAs were most common in the intergenic regions (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a result from the genomic distribution analysis by size shown in the figure.

claim: 24 nt sRNAs were most common in the intergenic regions.
source: The genic regions of non-transposon genes held the highest number of 21 nt sRNAs, while 24 nt sRNAs were most common in the intergenic regions (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a result from the genomic distribution analysis by size shown in the figure.

claim: sRNAs of 21 nt in genic regions were mostly derived from the exon of non-transposon genes.
source: sRNAs of 21 nt in genic regions were mostly derived from the exon of non-transposon genes, while 24 nt sRNAs in genic regions were mainly from the intron of non-transposon genes (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a result from the genic region distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: 24 nt sRNAs in genic regions were mainly from the intron of non-transposon genes.
source: sRNAs of 21 nt in genic regions were mostly derived from the exon of non-transposon genes, while 24 nt sRNAs in genic regions were mainly from the intron of non-transposon genes (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a result from the genic region distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The 24-nt sRNAs mainly consist of endogenous heterochromatic siRNAs and tend to be produced from repeats and transposable elements as well as intergenic regions.
source: The 24-nt sRNAs mainly consist of endogenous heterochromatic siRNAs (Axtell, 2013) and tend to be produced from repeats and transposable elements as well as intergenic regions (Chen, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The 24-nt sRNAs are components of the epigenome that target the homologous genomic regions for de novo DNA methylation through RNA-directed DNA methylation to maintain genome stability by transcriptional gene silencing.
source: The 24-nt sRNAs are components of the epigenome that target the homologous genomic regions for de novo DNA methylation through RNA-directed DNA methylation to maintain genome stability by transcriptional gene silencing (Groszmann et al., 2011a, 2013; Pooggin, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A total of 87.9% of s-traits were 24 nt.
source: A total of 87.9% of s-traits were 24 nt (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the s-trait size distribution analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The s-traits mainly originated from the intergenic regions, 2-kb upstream, and genic regions of non-transposon genes.
source: The s-traits mainly originated from the intergenic regions, 2-kb upstream, and genic regions of non-transposon genes (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a result from the genomic distribution analysis of s-traits shown in the figure.

claim: The number of s-traits derived from the 2-kb upstream of non-transposon genes was more than twice of the number of s-traits in genic regions of non-transposon genes.
source: Although the 2-kb upstream and the genic regions of non-transposon genes contained almost equal number of sRNAs (Figure 1B), the number of s-traits derived from the 2-kb upstream of non-transposon genes was more than twice of the number of s-traits in genic regions of non-transposon genes (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a comparative result from the genomic distribution analysis shown in the figures.

claim: A total of 3,739,873 correlation coefficients involving 15,078 genes and 96,914 s-traits were obtained for s-traits originated from the same gene.
source: A total of 3,739,873 correlation coefficients involving 15,078 genes and 96,914 s-traits were obtained, 2,593,503 (69.3%) and 507,528 (13.6%) of which were contributed by 2278 s-traits from genes LOC_Os03g01360 and 1008 s-traits from LOC_Os07g01240, respectively (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis.

claim: 2,593,503 (69.3%) correlation coefficients were contributed by 2278 s-traits from gene LOC_Os03g01360.
source: A total of 3,739,873 correlation coefficients involving 15,078 genes and 96,914 s-traits were obtained, 2,593,503 (69.3%) and 507,528 (13.6%) of which were contributed by 2278 s-traits from genes LOC_Os03g01360 and 1008 s-traits from LOC_Os07g01240, respectively (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis.

claim: 507,528 (13.6%) correlation coefficients were contributed by 1008 s-traits from gene LOC_Os07g01240.
source: A total of 3,739,873 correlation coefficients involving 15,078 genes and 96,914 s-traits were obtained, 2,593,503 (69.3%) and 507,528 (13.6%) of which were contributed by 2278 s-traits from genes LOC_Os03g01360 and 1008 s-traits from LOC_Os07g01240, respectively (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis.

claim: The correlation coefficients naturally fell into three classes: strong negative correlations, no correlation, and strong positive correlations with obvious dividing points at −0.3 and 0.3.
source: The correlation coefficients naturally fell into three classes: strong negative correlations, no correlation, and strong positive correlations with obvious dividing points at −0.3 and 0.3 (Figure 2A), which were far above 0.25, the threshold for statistical significance at p < 0.05 determined by simulation data.
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis shown in the figure.

claim: 85.8% of strong correlations (positive or negative) were contributed by s-traits originated from LOC_Os03g01360.
source: While 85.8% of these strong correlations (positive or negative) were contributed by s-traits originated from LOC_Os03g01360 (Figure 2B), most of s-traits originated from gene LOC_Os07g01240 showed low (or no) correlations with each other (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Most of s-traits originated from gene LOC_Os07g01240 showed low (or no) correlations with each other.
source: While 85.8% of these strong correlations (positive or negative) were contributed by s-traits originated from LOC_Os03g01360 (Figure 2B), most of s-traits originated from gene LOC_Os07g01240 showed low (or no) correlations with each other (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The expression values of s-traits originated from the same regions of the remaining 15,076 genes in the whole genome were mostly slightly positively correlated.
source: Although the expression values of s-traits originated from the same regions of the remaining 15,076 genes in the whole genome were mostly slightly positively correlated, the correlation coefficients were significantly distinct from that of the simulation of random data (Mann–Whitney U test, p-value <2.2e-16, Figure 2D), indicating various degrees of correlations.
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis with statistical testing shown in the figure.

claim: Expression correlations between s-traits of the same size were stronger than that between s-traits of different sizes.
source: We found that the correlations were affected by the sizes of s-traits (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). Expression correlations between s-traits of the same size were stronger than that between s-traits of different sizes.
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis by size shown in the figure.

claim: The expression correlations between 21-nt sRNAs and 25-nt sRNAs from the same genes were very weak.
source: In particular, the expression correlations between 21-nt sRNAs and 25-nt sRNAs from the same genes were very weak.
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis by size.

claim: The correlations between overlapped s-traits were slightly stronger than that between s-traits not overlapping with each other.
source: The correlations between overlapped s-traits were slightly stronger than that between s-traits not overlapping with each other (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis by overlap shown in the figure.

claim: An sRNA island was defined as a genomic region composed of consecutive genomic positions matched by at least 30× sRNA read coverage.
source: An sRNA island was defined as a genomic region composed of consecutive genomic positions matched by at least 30× sRNA read coverage.
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study.

claim: Nearby sRNA islands resided within 1000 nt from each other were merged and regarded as the same sRNA cluster.
source: Nearby sRNA islands resided within 1000 nt from each other were merged and regarded as the same sRNA cluster.
evidence: This is a methodological definition used in the study.

claim: 80,362 sRNA clusters were recovered with an average size of 1927 bp (ranging from 51 bp to 47,021 bp).
source: As a result, 80,362 sRNA clusters were recovered with an average size of 1927 bp (ranging from 51 bp to 47,021 bp) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 4 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sRNA cluster analysis.

claim: 46,293 (57.6%) sRNA clusters overlapped with genic regions.
source: A total of 46,293 (57.6%) sRNA clusters overlapped with genic regions, 23,143 (28.8%) of which were entirely derived from genic regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sRNA cluster genomic distribution analysis.

claim: 23,143 (28.8%) sRNA clusters were entirely derived from genic regions.
source: A total of 46,293 (57.6%) sRNA clusters overlapped with genic regions, 23,143 (28.8%) of which were entirely derived from genic regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sRNA cluster genomic distribution analysis.

claim: 50,139 (62.4%) sRNA clusters were determined as sc-traits.
source: A total of 50,139 (62.4%) sRNA clusters were determined as sc-traits, 34,762 of which were expressed in all of the 98 IMF2s.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sc-trait analysis.

claim: 34,762 sc-traits were expressed in all of the 98 IMF2s.
source: A total of 50,139 (62.4%) sRNA clusters were determined as sc-traits, 34,762 of which were expressed in all of the 98 IMF2s.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sc-trait analysis.

claim: A total of 4,282,587 correlation coefficients involving 21,571 sRNA clusters and 157,994 s-traits were obtained for s-traits originating from the same sRNA clusters.
source: A total of 4,282,587 correlation coefficients involving 21,571 sRNA clusters and 157,994 s-traits were obtained, 72.5% of which were contributed by s-traits from clusters chr03-261504-273325 and chr07-136331-141317 (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis.

claim: 72.5% of correlation coefficients were contributed by s-traits from clusters chr03-261504-273325 and chr07-136331-141317.
source: A total of 4,282,587 correlation coefficients involving 21,571 sRNA clusters and 157,994 s-traits were obtained, 72.5% of which were contributed by s-traits from clusters chr03-261504-273325 and chr07-136331-141317 (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis.

claim: 35,819 (54.2%) mRNAs were expressed in none of the 98 IMF2s.
source: An mRNA with FPKM value ≥1 was regarded as expressed; 35,819 (54.2%) mRNAs were expressed in none of the 98 IMF2s, while 16,849 (25.5%) were expressed in all the 98 IMF2s.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mRNA expression analysis.

claim: 16,849 (25.5%) mRNAs were expressed in all the 98 IMF2s.
source: An mRNA with FPKM value ≥1 was regarded as expressed; 35,819 (54.2%) mRNAs were expressed in none of the 98 IMF2s, while 16,849 (25.5%) were expressed in all the 98 IMF2s.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the mRNA expression analysis.

claim: A total of 24,987 e-traits were obtained from a total of 66,123 mRNAs in the whole genome.
source: An mRNA identified as expressed in more than 25 of the 98 IMF2s was regarded as an e-trait. In this way, a total of 24,987 e-traits were obtained from a total of 66,123 mRNAs in the whole genome.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the e-trait analysis.

claim: A total of 77,640 correlation coefficients were obtained, involving 9968 mRNAs and 56,185 s-traits for s-traits and their mother genes.
source: To assess whether sRNAs and their mother genes were transcribed together, the correlation coefficients of the expression values of s-traits and their mother genes were calculated. A total of 77,640 correlation coefficients were obtained, involving 9968 mRNAs and 56,185 s-traits.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis.

claim: 13,749 (17.7%) correlations between s-traits and their mother genes were strong correlations (above 0.3 or below −0.3).
source: Among all these correlations, 13,749 (17.7%) were strong correlations (above 0.3 or below −0.3, based on a threshold of 0.23 determined by simulation data with p < 0.05).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis.

claim: 45.6% of strong correlations between s-traits and their mother genes were contributed by gene LOC_Os03g01360.
source: However, 45.6% of these strong correlations were again contributed by gene LOC_Os03g01360 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the correlation analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The correlation coefficients involving rest of the genes in the whole genome were centered around zero.
source: The correlation coefficients involving rest of the genes in the whole genome were centered around zero (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from the correlation analysis shown in the figure.

claim: A total of 70,858 sQTLs were recovered for 66,649 s-traits with a false discovery rate (FDR) set at 5%.
source: With a false discovery rate (FDR) set at 5%, a total of 70,858 sQTLs were recovered for 66,649 s-traits (Supplementary file 7 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL mapping analysis.

claim: Expression variations of s-traits explained by local-sQTLs were substantially higher than that by distant-sQTLs.
source: Expression variations of s-traits explained by local-sQTLs were substantially higher than that by distant-sQTLs (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from the QTL analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The LOD values for 80.4% of the local-sQTLs and 34.5% of distant-sQTLs were larger than 10.
source: The LOD values for 80.4% of the local-sQTLs and 34.5% of distant-sQTLs were larger than 10.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL analysis.

claim: A total of 22,263 scQTLs including 11,476 local-scQTLs and 10,787 distant-sQTLs were recovered for 20,049 sc-traits.
source: A total of 22,263 scQTLs including 11,476 local-scQTLs and 10,787 distant-sQTLs were recovered for 20,049 sc-traits utilizing the same definitions of local- and distant-QTLs (Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 7 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL mapping analysis.

claim: A total of 6423 eQTLs were recovered for 6123 e-traits with an FDR set at 5%.
source: With an FDR set at 5%, a total of 6423 eQTLs were recovered for 6123 e-traits (Supplementary file 7 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL mapping analysis.

claim: 2964 local-eQTLs and 3459 distant-eQTLs were detected.
source: As a result, 2964 local-eQTLs (shown in the diagonal of Figure 4—figure supplement 6) and 3459 distant-eQTLs (off-diagonal of Figure 4—figure supplement 6) were detected (Supplementary file 7 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL mapping analysis.

claim: Local-QTLs regulating the expression of large numbers of traits were observed for s-traits and sc-traits but not for e-traits.
source: Local-QTLs regulating the expression of large numbers of traits were observed for s-traits and sc-traits but not for e-traits (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 6), probably due to the consecutive transcription of sRNAs and sRNA clusters, which was distinct from the transcription of mRNAs.
evidence: This is a comparative result from the QTL analysis shown in the figures.

claim: A total of 1660 s-traits were regulated by a single local-sQTL (Bin358) on chromosome 3.
source: In the extreme case, a total of 1660 s-traits were regulated by a single local-sQTL (Bin358) on chromosome 3 (Supplementary file 8 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL analysis.

claim: 514 s-traits were regulated by a single distant-sQTL (Bin1209).
source: A total of 15 bins were identified as distant-sQTLs, each of which regulated more than 200 s-traits; in one case, 514 s-traits were regulated by a single distant-sQTL (Bin1209).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL analysis.

claim: A total of 15,037 QTLs, 11,781 of which were local-sQTLs, were obtained for 14,139 s-traits expressed in only one of the two parents.
source: A total of 15,037 QTLs, 11,781 of which were local-sQTLs, were obtained for 14,139 of these s-traits.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the QTL analysis of parent-specific s-traits.

claim: The proportion of local-sQTLs for s-traits expressed in only one parent was significantly higher than the whole genome average level.
source: This proportion was significantly higher than the whole genome average level (Fisher's exact test, p value <2.2e-16), implying that the expression variations of these s-traits were mostly controlled by local polymorphisms.
evidence: This is a result from statistical testing of the QTL data.

claim: 40 bins were identified as hotspots for s-traits.
source: 40 bins were identified as hotspots for s-traits (Supplementary file 8 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015], Figure 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the hotspot analysis.

claim: 132 and 129 bins were identified as local-sQTL and distant-sQTL hotspots, respectively.
source: A total of 132 and 129 bins were identified as local-sQTL and distant-sQTL hotspots, respectively (Supplementary file 8 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015], Figure 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the hotspot analysis.

claim: 21 bins were both s-trait and local-sQTL hotspots.
source: 21 bins were both s-trait and local-sQTL hotspots, while 64 bins were both local-sQTL and distant-sQTL hotspots (Supplementary file 8 in Dryad [Wang et al., 2015], Figure 5)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the hotspot overlap analysis.

claim: 64 bins were both local-sQTL and distant-sQTL hotspots.

claim: Local elements are a major regulatory factor for sRNA variation.

claim: Quantitative variation for a large portion of sRNAs transcribed from genic regions did not share the genetic control of the expression with the corresponding mother genes.
source: Our results showed that quantitative variation for a large portion of sRNAs transcribed from genic regions did not share the genetic control of the expression with the corresponding mother genes, although by common sense those sRNAs have to be transcribed along and regulated by the promoters of the mother genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the QTL and correlation analysis.

claim: The transcription of sRNAs may be regulated by their own promoters, independent of the mother genes.
source: The results of Monteys et al. (2010) and Ozsolak et al. (2008) suggested that the transcription of sRNAs may also be regulated by their own promoters, independent of the mother genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion from previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Independent transcription of the sRNAs might be a common phenomenon, rather than only special circumstances.
source: The widespread occurrence of such independent genetic controls between the sRNAs and the mother genes suggested that independent transcription of the sRNAs might be a common phenomenon, rather than only special circumstances.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of genetic controls.

claim: Studies in sRNA pathways in Arabidopsis showed that DCL2 is responsible for the synthesis of 22 nt or 24 nt siRNAs.

evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Negative dominance of sRNA levels was also observed in comparative sRNA profiling of hybrids relative to the parents in crosses of rice and Arabidopsis.

evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies cited in the manuscript.
